title: fix(runtime): on the standalone server, an anonymous request whose JSON body cannot be parsed gets the domain's 401, not the transport's 400
body:
Fixes #24151

Clause-②: no

## What

On the standalone server (`os dev`, `os serve`: `HonoServerPlugin` + the dispatcher plugin), every mount in `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts` that handed `dispatch()` `req.body` now hands it `deferRequestBody(req)`, and each domain reads the body with `readDispatchedBody(body)` once its anonymous decision (ADR-0138 D2) has admitted the caller. An anonymous caller's answer no longer depends on whether its JSON body parses; an admitted caller with an unparseable body still gets the transport's `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

- `packages/runtime/src/deferred-request-body.ts` (new, module-private to the package, not exported from the index): the two halves. `deferRequestBody(req)` returns a value that holds the request and reads nothing; `readDispatchedBody(body)` reads `req.body` for a deferred value and returns any other value unchanged (what `createHonoApp`, tests and internal callers hand `dispatch()`). A deferred value read WITHOUT being resolved throws an `UnresolvedRequestBodyRead` error on every trap, so a domain that forgets the resolve fails loudly at its first read instead of acting on an invented empty body.
- `dispatcher-plugin.ts`: 24 call sites, `req.body` becomes `deferRequestBody(req)` (the card's 20, plus 4 the card's grep missed, below). One note at the shared `sendResult` / `errorResponse` helpers says why.
- Nine domains, one statement each, right after the anonymous decision: `analytics`, `mcp`, `keys`, `notifications`, `automation` (after the inbound-hook hand-off, which verifies raw bytes and never reads a parsed body), `actions`, `ai`, `packages`, `security`. `ai` decides per route: an admitted caller's body is read at the domain-wide decision, and an anonymous caller a route's `auth: false` admits has it read in the route loop.
- Untouched: `packages/spec` (`IHttpRequest`'s body contract), `packages/adapters/hono`, `plugin-hono-server`'s adapter, PR #24244's fallback path, the domains' logic beyond when they read the body.

## H1: domain by domain (measured on a real socket, base `cbfa5e433`, head `8e9fd41b2`)

Anonymous request, `content-type: application/json`, body `{"name": "probe"` (closing brace missing). "Anonymous first?" is read in the domain's source on `cbfa5e433`.

| site(s) on `cbfa5e433` | domain | anonymous decided first? | base | head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `:1282` `POST /analytics/query`, `:1300` `POST /analytics/sql` | `analytics` | yes, first statement | 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` | 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` |
| `:1326` `/mcp` (POST, GET, DELETE) | `mcp` | **no**: `isMcpServerEnabled()` 404 and the service probe 501 come first (finding below) | 400 | 401 (MCP on and installed); 404 / 501 otherwise, body unread |
| `:1362` `/mcp/skill` (POST, GET, DELETE) | `mcp/skill` | no anonymous decision: public by design ("Served PUBLIC like `/discovery`") | 400 | 405 `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, its own answer to any non-GET |
| `:1395` `POST /keys`, `:1409` `/keys` (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) | `keys` | yes, first statement | 400 | 401 |
| `:1447` `POST /notifications/read`, `:1456` `POST /notifications/read/all` | `notifications` | yes, first statement | 400 | 401 |
| `:1676`–`:1857`, the nine `/automation` mounts | `automation` | yes, first statement | 400 | 401 |
| `:1947`, `:1955`, `:1963`, the three `POST /actions/...` shapes | `actions` | yes, first statement | 400 | 401 |
| `:1909` the `/ai/*` wildcards (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), not in the card's grep | `ai` | yes, decided once ahead of every capability answer; a route's `auth: false` opens it | 400 | 401 |
| `:1553` the `/packages` registrar (16 mounts), not in the card's grep | `packages` | yes, first statement | 400 | 401 |
| `:2006` `POST /security/_activation/:type/:name`, `:2020` `POST /security/permission-sets/:name/clone`, not in the card's grep | `security` | yes, first statement | 400 | 401 |

At base the same anonymous requests with a well-formed body answered 401 everywhere (405 on `/mcp/skill`): only the parse decided the 400. Base was measured on the unscoped prefix; the scoped (`/environments/:environmentId`) mounts are the same registrar code, and head pins both prefixes.

## H2, H3, H4

- **H2, partly falsified.** `createHonoApp` answers 401 because `readDispatchBody` hands `dispatch()` either the parsed value or `refusedOnRead(...)`: a Proxy over `Object.create(null)` whose every trap throws the refusal and records the read, which the arm then answers. Not a getter or a thunk. `dispatch()`'s `body` parameter is `any` and `dispatch()` never reads it (it passes it to `domainRoute.handler`), so the shape is accepted. But a standalone mount cannot build it: it can learn whether the body parsed only by reading `req.body`, the one door `IHttpRequest` declares, and that read IS the refusal. A lazily forwarding Proxy would have needed no domain change, but it is not faithful: `Array.isArray`, `typeof` and `== null` read the target, fixed at creation, so a JSON array (an MCP JSON-RPC batch; `@objectstack/mcp` passes `parsedBody` to the SDK, which branches on `Array.isArray`), `null` or a primitive would reach the domain as an object. So the domains read the body explicitly, one statement each.
- **H3, confirmed.** The adapter's `get body()` throws the refusal and records `refusedBodyRead`; the adapter then answers that refusal whatever the handler did. Deferring the read into the domain needs no adapter change: all anonymous pins are green with `adapter.ts` untouched.
- **H4, confirmed with two named exceptions.** A signed-in caller with the same body gets `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, message "The request body could not be parsed as JSON …" (the transport's refusal, unchanged) on every site whose domain reads a body once it admits the caller. Exceptions, both answers the domain gives without reading a body, as on `createHonoApp`: `/mcp/skill` (its 405; base answered 400, measured) and `/mcp` where MCP is switched off or not installed (404 / 501; base answered 400 by construction, the mount reading the body before `dispatch()`).

## The four mounts outside the card's grep (bounded in-place fix)

The card's grep `dispatcher\.dispatch\([^)]*req\.body` stops at the first `)`, so it missed the `/ai/*` wildcard (`method.toUpperCase()` precedes `req.body`) and the three registrars that spell the call over several lines (`/packages`, `/security/_activation`, `/security/permission-sets/:name/clone`). Same defect class, same mechanical change, same file, same gate families. Evidence, base `cbfa5e433`, anonymous: `POST /ai/chat`, `PUT` and `PATCH /ai/conversations/c1`, `POST /packages`, `PATCH /packages/pkg_x`, `PATCH /packages/pkg_x/enable`, `POST /packages/pkg_x/publish`, `POST /packages/pkg_x/rollback`, `POST /security/_activation/permission_set/ps_x`, `POST /security/permission-sets/ps_x/clone`: each 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` with the unparseable body, 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` with the well-formed one. Head: 401 for both. Pinned below.

Two `req.body` reads remain in the file, both deliberately: the service-emitted route mount (the mount decides `route.auth` before it reads the body, so an anonymous answer never depends on it), and the declarative-endpoint fallback, which is not a `dispatch()` mount (see Acceptance notes).

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-body-after-anonymous-floor.hono.integration.test.ts` (new): real Hono socket, `LiteKernel`, both prefixes for the registrars `enableProjectScoping` mounts twice. 60 URLs, two pins each: anonymous + unparseable gets the domain's anonymous answer in the dispatcher's envelope, equal to the anonymous + well-formed answer; signed-in + unparseable gets the transport's refusal (or `/mcp/skill`'s 405). 120 tests.
- `packages/runtime/src/deferred-request-body.test.ts` (new): the value's own contract, 5 tests: nothing is read until it is resolved; resolving returns the exact value (object, array, `null`, string, number, boolean); the transport's refusal propagates as the same object; values it did not defer pass through untouched; an unresolved read throws `UnresolvedRequestBodyRead` on every trap and never reads the request.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 415 files passed, 6536 tests passed, 19 skipped (run at `bde3873ed`; `8e9fd41b2` adds only the changeset).
- `--project repo` (it reads `dispatcher-plugin.ts` as text): 3 files, 808 tests passed at `8e9fd41b2`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0; `check:test-typecheck` OK, the two new test files add no debt.

**Ablation (one, as asked).** `deferRequestBody` mutated to `return req.body;` (eager read again) through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: anchor 1 to 0, blob `7d7452c90112` to `dfaf76e93a8e`. The test imports `./dispatcher-plugin.js` from `src` by relative path, so no `dist/` is on the path. Result: 62 failed, 58 passed of 120. Red: all 60 anonymous pins, and the two signed-in `/mcp/skill` pins, whose expected answer is the domain's own 405, which an eager read pre-empts with 400. Green: the 58 signed-in refusal controls. Restore proven: blob back to `7d7452c90112` equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates (at `8e9fd41b2`)

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: 65 commands. 64 exit 0. 1 NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (it reads every package's `dist/`; only the runtime closure is built here). `--ran` with exit codes: "65 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 64 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED". Also, for the roster families whose list lives under a changed directory: `check:route-ledger-census`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`, each exit 0. `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the 13 changed `.ts` files: exit 0. The repo-wide `pnpm lint`, the type-check lanes, Test Core, Build Core and dogfood are CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- **`/mcp` does not decide anonymous first (H1).** `handleMcpRequest` answers `404` when `OS_MCP_SERVER_ENABLED` is off and `501` when no MCP service is installed, both ahead of its `401`. Measured in process on the standalone composition: anonymous `POST /api/v1/mcp` answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with no MCP service and `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` with MCP off, for a well-formed and an unparseable body alike. Not changed here: the dispatch order says a domain that does not decide anonymous first is a finding, not something to add a check for.
- **The declarative-endpoint fallback reads the body before its own decisions.** The fallback seam builds `execution.request.body` from `req.body` before `runAppEndpointStep` matches an endpoint or applies `authRequired`. Measured: anonymous `POST /api/v1/apps/ns/x` answers `400 INVALID_REQUEST` with an unparseable body and `404 ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND` with a well-formed one; signed in, the same. A declared `authRequired: true` endpoint was not driven, so whether an anonymous caller gets 400 where 401 is owed there is inferred, NOT MEASURED. Not a `dispatch()` mount, so outside this change.
- `/mcp/skill` is public by design and reads no body, so its row pins its own 405 rather than 401.
- A signed-in caller's answer moved only where the domain answers without reading a body (the two H4 exceptions); everywhere else it is byte-for-byte what base answered.
